dimensions.assessment: Directly affects members of the Armed Forces nearing separation, military spouses, and personnel within the Department of Defense, Department of Labor, and Department of Veterans Affairs.
dimensions.evidence: members of the Armed Forces who are transitioning to civilian life

dimensions.assessment: Extends transitional health care from 180 to 270 days, standardizes counseling paths, and adds mandatory financial planning and at-risk outreach.
dimensions.evidence: extends transitional health care for members separating from service to 270 days

dimensions.assessment: Extends health care coverage duration and expands program eligibility, implying increased administrative and health service costs without specifying a total dollar amount.
Amends titles 10 and 38 of the United States Code regarding pre-separation counseling, tracking systems, pilot programs, and inter-agency coordination.
dimensions.evidence: To amend titles 10 and 38, United States Code, to make improvements to certain programs

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes to transition programs, with specific multi-year reporting requirements and a three-year pilot program.

missing_information: Estimated budget outlays for extending transitional health care and expanding pilot programs.
importance_detail.rationale: Modifies transition assistance, counseling durations, transitional health care, and reporting requirements for members of the Armed Forces separating to civilian life.
